MaxMart Retail - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the MaxMart Retail Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, to ask a question, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad. Please also note, today's event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, and thank you for joining us today to discuss MaxMart Retail's results for the Q3 2024. Joining me on today’s call are Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Emily Chen, Chief Financial Officer; and David Ruiz, Chief Merchandising Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements, which are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

With that, I’ll turn the call over to Johnathan.

Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I’m pleased to report MaxMart Retail's performance for the Q3. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities and delivered solid results despite the challenging macroeconomic environment.

In terms of our overall performance, comparable store sales grew 5.3%, driven by traffic up 1.8% and average ticket up 3.4%, with particular strength in home goods and essentials offsetting some apparel softness. E-commerce sales accelerated 18.2% year-over-year, representing 28.4% of total sales and outpacing brick-and-mortar comps significantly. Store performance remained resilient, highlighted by record inventory turnover of 5.8 times, down to 63 days inventory outstanding, and inventories reduced 18% to $1.2 billion even as comps rose 12% in some areas. Our marketing initiatives, especially digital, delivered a blended ROAS of 5.8 times, driving incremental store traffic and BOPIS orders. Finally, supply chain optimizations, including AI forecasting and omnichannel fulfillment, have positioned us for margin expansion.

We are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Emily to provide more details on our financial results.

Emily Chen, Chief Financial Officer:
Thank you, Johnathan. Good morning. I'll provide a more detailed review of our financial performance for the Q3.

Our total revenue for the quarter was $1.55 billion, a 4.2% increase compared to the same period last year. Gross margin was 37.8%, reflecting a 50 basis point decline primarily due to elevated markdown activity amid cautious consumer spending, partially offset by inventory optimization gains of 140 basis points from lower markdowns and faster turns. Operating expenses were $450 million, representing 29% of revenue, as we invested in digital capabilities and store labor. Net income was $110 million, or $0.78 per share. We generated $180 million in cash flow from operations. Inventory levels are currently down 18% to $1.2 billion, with days inventory outstanding at 63 days, supporting working capital release of $250 million.

Let me expand on some key drivers. First, turning to gross margin performance, which landed at 37.8%. Elevated markdown activity contributed to the pressure, with our markdown rate hitting 18.4% of net sales, up from 14.2% last year, equating to about $285 million on quarterly sales. This directly shaved roughly 110 basis points off margins, alongside higher shrink at 1.8% and some mix shifts away from private labels. Apparel drove 62% of markdowns at 24.1% of category sales, hit by softer casual denim and activewear sell-through as middle-income shoppers traded down with 3% comp traffic pullback. Footwear was more resilient at 12.8%, thanks to Nike and Adidas exclusives, while home goods rose to 16.5% from excess seasonal stock due to warm fall weather.

Regionally, Northeast and Midwest stores—about 35% of our 1,800 locations—saw markdowns at 21.2% of sales, 250 basis points above average, tied to mild weather hurting outerwear and flat comps similar to urban softness at peers. Sunbelt areas like Texas and Florida, 45% of doors, managed 15.7% markdowns with 4.2% comp growth from tourism and back-to-school. Ending inventories up 8% year-over-year at $1.2 billion, or 12.4 weeks supply, down from 14 weeks prior, with apparel at 16 weeks prompting clearance to make room for spring.

We're responding aggressively. Rolled out AI-driven dynamic pricing via Blue Yonder partnership across 85% of stores, optimizing cadences with sell-through, competitor data from Placer.ai, and weather, improving clearance velocity 15% and days-to-sell from 45 to 39. Vendor scorecards with Levi's and Under Armour now cover 22% of Q4 intake for markdown reimbursements, up from 12%. Expect markdowns to ease to 16-17% in Q4 as inventories hit 11 weeks, delivering 50-75 basis points gross margin expansion on flat comps. Full-price sell-through at 72%, up from 68%, with private labels targeting 28% of sales at 45%+ margins.

Shifting to e-commerce sales growth year-over-year at 18.2%, outpacing total comps of 4.1% and store comps of 1.8%, our 11th straight double-digit quarter. E-commerce now 28.4% of net sales, up from 23.7%, with GMV at $1.42 billion, up 19.5%, from 12% traffic rise, 4.2% AOV growth to $128, and 2% conversion to 3.8%. Ex-FX, 19.8%. Mobile commerce, 62% of traffic, up 32% via progressive web app on BigCommerce Catalyst, cutting load times 45%, bounce to 38%, and speeding purchases 25%, especially impulse apparel under $50 up 41%.

By category, home and garden led at 25.6% growth from patio and grilling demand, with ship-from-store delivering 85% same/next-day from 1,800 locations. Apparel 16.8%, aided by 22% better online availability via store RFID. Electronics 9.4%, hurt by semis, but Sony PlayStation bundles up 150%. U.S. 76% of e-com, up 22.7%, Sun Belt adding $180 million GMV, California 35% e-com comps. Canada 14.2% with bilingual AI chat resolving 70% queries, cutting abandonment 18%. Europe 8.9% on UK headwinds, but Dublin center ramping to $200 million throughput.

Pillars: Omnichannel fills 52% of orders, cutting last-mile to $4.20, e-com GM 42.3% vs. company 37.8%, 15% higher repeats. Personalization via Adobe ML predicts 85% next-bests, 22% AOV lift; Rewards app 18 million members, 12.5% push conversions. Marketplace added 1,200 SKUs like Yeti, $95 million or 7% GMV risk-free. CAC up 11% to $28 on ad costs, offset by 45% organic traffic. Q3 guide 15-17% growth, full-year $5.8 billion, penetration to 30% FY2026. Stores drive 22% e-com via QR/kiosks, e-com funnels 14% to stores.

On digital marketing effectiveness, amid 2.1% retail traffic decline per Placer.ai and inflation on discretionary, our $145 million spend up 18% YoY—22% of budget—delivered 5.8x blended ROAS, up from 4.2x, beating Target's 4.5x. Alloc: 42% search (Google/Bing, $1.47 CPC), 35% social (Meta/TikTok), 12% programmatic, rest Snapchat AR/SMS via Braze. Search 8.2x ROAS, social 4.1x with 28% conversion lift. CAC down 12% to $28, CLV $1,240 for digital vs. $980 traditional, 4.4x LTV:CAC.

Multi-touch attribution via GA4/Meridian CDP shows 62% incremental; geo ads within 5 miles lifted traffic 22%, "Cozy Home Refresh" drove 1.7 million visits, $285 million physical sales or 14% comps. Einstein AI segments 47 cohorts, DCO up CTR 34%; geo-holdouts confirm 16% retargeting lift. Pinterest AR up intent 41%, Google Nearby for local stock. U.S. 78% spend, urban 6.5x, Sun Belt 7.2x. Canada 5.2x, Quebec strong. Europe 4.3x, sustainability messaging up 32%. Omnichannel: 41% digital to store fills. Q4 $160 million for 6.2x ROAS. Drove 24% EBITDA lift.

Before questions, a deeper look at traffic versus ticket. Q3 comps 5.3%, sixth straight positive, beating NRF 2.1%. Traffic +1.8%, ticket +3.4%. Apparel +4.1% (traffic +0.9%, ticket +3.2% via premium denim $89 AUR, bundling up units 2.7%). Home +7.2% (traffic +3.4%, ticket +3.7%, Quick Ship). Essentials +5.9% (traffic +1.2%, ticket +4.6%, beauty AUR +6.2%). Conversion 28.5%, dwell 22 min.

Regions: Southeast +8.2% (traffic +4.1%), Midwest flat traffic +5.7% ticket via 18% BOPIS. Northeast +1.9% (traffic -1.2%), West +4.7% balanced. Store 2.0 tech in 40%: AI scheduling +1.5ppt conversion, Instacart 8% traffic, SymphonyAI velocity +22%, Rewards +$4.20 ATV. BOPIS 22% fills. Traffic opportunity vs. 2019 peaks; H2 50 remodels. Q4 comps 3-5%, traffic 1-2%, ticket 2-3%.

Now on inventory optimization strategies, a cornerstone of StoreStrong 2025. Achieved 5.8x turnover, up from 4.2x vs. NRF 4.5x; DIO 63 days from 87, 27% better. Inventories down 18% to $1.2B despite 12% comps, boosting GM 140bps to 38.2% adjusted, markdowns 2.1% from 3.8%, freeing $250M working capital for remodels/digital DCs.

Strategies: AI demand sensing on Blue Yonder/SAP with 50 signals—POS, weather, confidence, Google Trends—cut apparel forecast error 35% to 12% SKU-store, holiday pre-buy down safety stock 22% for Levi's/Nike (15% assortments). Nowcasting from 500 ship-from-store hubs.

ABC/XYZ: A-items (20% SKUs, 80% sales like iPhones/TVs) weekly JIT; B/C (60% inventory, 15% sales like KitchenAid) VMI with P&G/Unilever, costs down 22%. Northeast RFID from Zebra cut OOS 40%, shrinkage 1.2% vs. 1.8%.

BOPIS 28% digital sales from 18%, Manhattan WMS in 1,200 stores, dark store reserves 10-15% Sonos. Geospatial: California +20% patio to coastal, Midwest trim appliances 15%, dynamic slotting GE fridges.

Tech: Honeywell IoT 99.2% accuracy in 40 DCs, no recounts save $15M. IBM blockchain perishables cut lead 3 days vs. Red Sea +25% freight. 10 MFCs Texas/Florida Alert robots -30% labor, 99.8% pick.

Regional: Southeast +10% safety generators NOAA, sell-through 112%; Canada -25% lumber CAD weakness/Home Hardware VMI. Rural supercenters +15% depth John Deere, adjusted leads.

Ahead: $150M FY25 AI scale, 6.5x turnover, 55 DIO, 200bps GM, 98% in-stock. Mitigate tariffs nearshoring Mexico +30%.

We are maintaining a strong balance sheet and are well positioned to invest in our growth initiatives.

Now, I'd like to hand it over to David, our Chief Merchandising Officer, to discuss our new product lines.

David Ruiz, Chief Merchandising Officer:
Thank you, Emily. This quarter, we launched our EcoHome Essentials line, featuring sustainable bedding, rugs, and furniture made with recycled materials and eco-linen blends. It has seen exceptional early traction, with sell-through exceeding 95% in test markets and contributing 7% to home category comps, driven by strong digital personalization and in-store AR try-ons. Customer feedback highlights the premium quality and green credentials, aligning with EU Green Deal trends and U.S. sustainability demand. We are excited about the potential of this new product and other upcoming launches like expanded activewear collaborations.

Now, let's open the line for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. As a reminder, to ask a question, press star one. Our first question comes from Mike Thompson with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Mike Thompson (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of inflation on your sales?

Johnathan Hale:
Thanks, Mike. Inflation continues to pressure middle-income consumers, leading to some trade-down in apparel where we saw softer traffic, but our ticket resilience from premium private labels and essentials offset that. Overall, it contributed to the balanced traffic and ticket growth we discussed, and our digital marketing geo-targeting helped drive incremental visits despite broader retail foot traffic declines.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen (JPMorgan):
What are your expectations for same-store sales growth in the next quarter?

Emily Chen:
Hi Lisa. For Q4, we expect comps of 3% to 5%, with traffic 1% to 2% and ticket 2% to 3%, supported by holiday ramps, moderating markdowns, and e-commerce synergies funneling to stores. This assumes stable sentiment, though macro risks like tariffs are mitigated by our sourcing shifts.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Robert Patel with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Robert Patel (Barclays):
Can you elaborate on the supply chain improvements?

Johnathan Hale:
Absolutely, Robert. Our inventory optimizations are central, with AI forecasting reducing errors 35%, VMI for B/C items cutting costs 22%, and IoT/blockchain trimming lead times amid disruptions. Omnichannel BOPIS at 28% of digital and MFCs boosting accuracy to 99.8% have enhanced fulfillment, supporting faster turns and margin gains while tailoring regionally, like buffers in hurricane zones.

Operator:
Thank you. That concludes today's question and answer session.

Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, we are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our long-term strategy. Thank you for your continued support.

Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations:
This concludes today's call. Thank you for joining us.
